title: Five Principles of Effective Negotiation
subtitle: Keep these principles in mind — they may help you during your negotiation.
body: Below are five principles that research has shown lead to better outcomes in negotiation. Read them carefully and try to apply them during your practice.

principles.title: Separate the people from the problem
principles.description: Keep the relationship separate from the substance. Try to understand the other side's perspective, acknowledge their emotions, and listen carefully. Attacking the person makes agreement harder, even if you win the argument.

principles.title: Focus on interests, not positions
principles.description: Try to understand why each side wants what they want — not just what they are asking for. The reasons behind a demand often reveal room for agreement.

principles.title: Invent options for mutual gain
principles.description: Look for creative solutions that could make both sides better off before deciding how to divide what's on the table. The goal is to expand the pie, not just split it.

principles.title: Insist on objective criteria
principles.description: Look for an independent standard that both sides can accept, such as market rates, precedent, or expert opinion. Agreeing on a fair basis for the decision makes it easier for both sides to say yes.

principles.title: Know your best alternative
principles.description: Know your best option if this negotiation fails. This is your walk-away point. The stronger your alternative, the more confidently you can negotiate, and the clearer you will be about when to walk away.
